S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor, with onset typically within 3 months of the stressor and clinically significant distress or functional impairment out of proportion to what would be expected. It often presents with anxiety, low mood, or mixed disturbance of emotions and conduct, but does not meet full criteria for another mental disorder and does not represent a normal bereavement reaction. The course is usually self-limited, resolving within 6 months after the stressor or its consequences have ended, though it can become chronic if stressors persist. Clinically, it is distinguished from normative stress reactions by its impact on social, occupational, or academic functioning and from major depressive or anxiety disorders by its subthreshold, stressor-linked symptom profile and time course.

patient.stressor: About six weeks ago, Lula’s husband was hospitalized unexpectedly after a minor stroke, and she suddenly became his primary caregiver while he recovered at home. Accustomed to planning church events and mentoring youth on a predictable schedule, she found herself juggling medication schedules, follow-up appointments in Macon, and physical therapy visits, all while trying to keep up with choir rehearsals and her commitments at the senior center. Over the following month, her carefully structured routines around gardening, quilting, and church work began to unravel, and she started backing out of activities she normally anchored for others, which worried her pastor and quilting circle. When she realized she was missing bill deadlines and couldn’t bring herself to organize the upcoming church potluck—something she had done for years—her daughter urged her to see a mental health professional through the clinic attached to the hospital’s stroke program.
patient.chief_complaint: “Ever since my husband’s stroke, I just haven’t been handling everything the way I usually do, and I feel like I’m not coping with all these changes.”

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Since my husband’s stroke, I feel like I’m constantly on edge and worn thin—snapping at people from church, forgetting simple things like when his pills are due, and then lying awake at night worrying I’m failing him and letting everything else in my life fall apart.

add_requirements.within_3_months_of_stressor: I started feeling this way within a week or two of bringing my husband home from the hospital, once all the appointments and caregiving routines really fell on my shoulders.
add_requirements.within_6_months_after_stressor_ends: The social worker at the clinic told me that once my husband is more independent again and the follow-up visits slow down, this rough patch should settle down within a few months instead of dragging on indefinitely.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: In the past month I’ve had to back out of leading the church potluck and several choir rehearsals, and I’ve even missed paying a couple of bills on time because I can’t keep up the way I used to.
add_requirements.duration: These problems with feeling overwhelmed, irritable, and unable to keep up have been going on for about a month now, ever since we got my husband home from the hospital.
